name: Al-A'sha
bio: Maymun ibn Qays, also known as Abu Basir, belonged to the Qays ibn Tha'laba branch of Bakr ibn Wa'il. From Manfuha in al-Yamama he travelled to Arab and Persian courts to perform poems for their rulers. Al-Zirikli connects his epithet “the cymbal player of the Arabs” with his habit of singing his verse, and the name al-A'sha with his failing eyesight. He lived into the Islamic period and died at Manfuha in 7 AH (629 CE), according to al-Zirikli.
